program.notes: let_me_buy (letmebuy.app) — a storefront program: a merchant stands up a store, lists products, and buyers pay in an SPL token by scanning a QR code. ONE PDA per store carries everything: receipts = ['receipts', store_name] (store_name is an instruction ARGUMENT, utf8), and the account holds the products vec, the receipts vec, total_purchases, authority, telegram_channel_id, details and bump. Every one of the eight instructions takes that same account, writable — which is what makes the lifecycle a chain rather than eight unrelated calls, and why product_name is never a seed. Derivation order is trivial (receipts depends on nothing but the store name) and the two associated-token accounts depend only on caller-supplied owner/mint, so nothing here needs a chain read to build. Instruction account lists, in IDL order: initialize(store_name) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer), system_program]; add_product(store_name, name, price:u64) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer), mint, system_program]; make_purchase(store_name, product_name, table_number:u8) = [receipts(w), signer(w,signer), authority(w), mint, sender_token_account(w), recipient_token_account(w), token_program, system_program, associated_token_program] (9); mark_as_delivered(_store_name, receipt_id:u64) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer)]; update_details(store_name, details) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer)]; update_telegram_channel(store_name, telegram_channel_id) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer)]; delete_product(store_name, product_name) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer), system_program]; delete_store(store_name) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer)]. THE JOIN THE IDL LOSES: mark_as_delivered's receipts account declares the seed arg path 'store_name', but that instruction's own args are named '_store_name' and 'receipt_id' — the seed points at an argument that does not exist in its instruction, so an IDL-driven deriver that resolves seed paths by arg name gets nothing for the one seed that selects the store. The recipe here binds by seed VALUE ('store_name' for all eight), and the wire arg for that call stays '_store_name'. SECOND TRAP: in make_purchase the store's `authority` is writable but NOT a signer — the merchant does not co-sign a sale; the program checks it against receipts.authority (6004 InvalidAuthority). The buyer pays from sender_token_account = ATA(signer, token_program, mint) and the store is credited at recipient_token_account = ATA(authority, token_program, mint) — same mint, same token program, different owner; deriving both from the same owner builds a purchase that pays the buyer back. token_program is pinned by the IDL to classic SPL Token (TokenkegQfeZyiNwAJbNbGKPFXCWuBvf9Ss623VQ5DA), so both ATAs are classic-Token ATAs and a Token-2022 mint has no path through this program. The currency is fixed per product by add_product's `mint` account (stored with price and decimals in the products vec); a make_purchase whose mint differs fails 6003 InvalidMint. delete_store refuses a store that still has products (6005 StoreNotEmpty) — delete_product first. Other errors: 6001 ProductAlreadyExists, 6002 ProductNotFound, 6006 ProductNameEmpty, 6007 StringTooLong, 6008 VectorLimitReached, 6009 InvalidStoreName. PROVENANCE: the Anchor IDL that states these recipes reached comprehension through the hosted project surface (a third-party mirror), not from the program's own on-chain IDL account, and the seeds were hand-authored into this config from it — so every entry is carried at `manual`, the reviewed-overlay tier, rather than `extracted`. Correctness of the receipts recipe is established separately, by a derived address matching a mainnet account the program owns; that is a chain fact pinned in tests/test_let_me_buy_config.py, and it is evidence, never a tier. No execute intent is wired for this program yet: it is comprehended for DERIVATION only.
